chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: "We lived spiritually": how the four-man section functioned
summary: Jones says the four men brought their personal lives onto their instruments and played from a spiritual ingredient.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: May I interject something in a serious note? That you'd have to delve in it very seriously? You got four peoples there. Milt, it takes a whole lot of living to do what we did. We never played with the band. We incorporated our personal lives and we put it on our instruments. Now that takes a whole lot of the life that Mr. Page had lived, Mr. Basie, Mr. Green, and myself. We took all of that. Now I want you to understand, Count Basie's band only functioned one way and it will only function one way today, because there's two ingredients that will make it function. I don't care what happened. No force is strong enough. We functioned morally, but I leave that alone. We started first spiritually. What it takes to get this spiritual ingredient, you have to live this spiritual ingredient. That leaves the moral intake on the outer fringe. We lived spiritually!
I don't believe in ghosts. You don't, but there is a Supreme Being -
Yes. But how you arrive - in every rhythm section I've ever been in the drummer is the controlling and the ruling force.
He is the force; he's the heart...
You and I have had more sessions together, as many sessions as any combinations of drummers and bass players in records; but your rhythm section was such a

tremendous force and I know that everything starts with the drums. But it seems as if that rhythm section, it was four guys that was all equal. It wasn't like one pushing one. You four functioned as one. How did that come out; what was the ruling force of this?
Spiritual. You must live spiritually. That's the motivating force.
